Novice

NOV-iss -- shares a root with 'novel,' meaning new. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Novice is a person who is new to and inexperienced in a particular activity or role.

As a novice in the kitchen, he burned the toast twice before breakfast was even ready.

Worked Example

A freshly hired lifeguard sits nervously at her first shift, unsure how to use the rescue equipment that her veteran coworkers handle without a second thought.

That inexperienced newcomer, still learning the basics everyone else already knows, is exactly what a novice is. Unlike 'expert,' a novice is only beginning.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

beginner: someone just starting to learn a skill

rookie: a person new to a job or activity

amateur: someone who does something without professional training

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

expert: a person with great skill or knowledge in a field

veteran: a person with long experience in a particular field

Where it sits · how formal or casual the label is — beginner → novice → rookie

beginner vs. novice: Beginner is a bit more neutral than novice -- beginner simply states someone is starting out, while novice can carry a slightly more formal, and sometimes mildly critical, tone about someone's inexperience.

rookie vs. novice: Rookie can feel more casual than novice: novice is a general, formal term for inexperience, while rookie specifically evokes a first-year athlete or employee still proving themselves.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — nov-

root — nov-: new (Latin (novus))

suffix — -ice

suffix — -ice: forming a noun; one who is (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Latin novus meant 'new,' and the suffix -ice forms a noun -- so a novice is literally 'a new one,' someone new to a skill, group, or role.

Use the root in a new word: novel
